cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic Songye nkishi power figure with metal-clad face, horn, beaded collar, raffia skirt, and medicine-laden abdominal cavity, all consistent with Songye ritual carving traditions.

physical.title: Male Figure (nkishi)
physical.medium_raw: Wood, glass beads, brass (including upholstery studs), copper alloy, iron alloy, raffia, reedbuck antelope horn, rawhide, animal hair, human teeth, organic material, minerals, and plant fibers
physical.summary: This figure's visual impact and workmanship suggest that an extended family––rather than an individual––used it. The raffia skirt around the waist and the blue and white beads are indicators of leadership. The metal appliqué covering the face and the metal blades that hedge the headgear refer to the blacksmith, a culture hero celebrated in a Songye myth narrating the formation of the state. The metal strips on the skeletal face are said to relate to lightning, signaling the figure's role as a powerful anti-sorcerer, but the contrast between white iron and red copper symbolically alludes to the ambivalent powers of the figure.

location.made_in_place: Africa, Central Africa, Democratic Republic of Congo, Songye-style carver and nganga (priest)
